## Curved surfaces and material finish in Windows 0.24.29

3D Studio samples the Hunyuan shape field at 320 intervals per axis and retains up to 155,000 triangles during compaction. It smooths small reconstruction irregularities across connected triangles before splitting the surface into texture atlases. Edges that turn sharply get less smoothing. The original TripoSR reconstruction path also receives the surface pass.

At oblique angles the front photo fades into the side texture. Inside that band, the baker samples the original photo per pixel. The GLB carries its material roughness through export. A glazed ceramic object takes a polish, while a prompt specifying a matte finish keeps a broad reflection. The studio preview uses soft room reflections that move as the model turns.

## Curved surfaces, Windows 0.24.29

Inspected the same cobalt owl with its textures disabled and enabled. Compared at fixed front, left and rear angles in the viewer. The refitted owl has 99,163 triangles, identical face connectivity, UVs and four identical embedded images. Its enclosed volume changed by about 0.15%. A controlled noisy sphere’s radius standard deviation fell from 0.0040 to 0.0015 and a sharp eight-corner cube retained its original vertex positions.

A separate Create run through the packaged Windows UI used Hunyuan3D 2.1 on the RTX 3060. It produced 146,912 triangles, four embedded image textures and a 5,660,692-byte GLB in 150.0 seconds. Verified the ceramic roughness on all exported materials, rotated the result, checked the exported fingerprint, and reopened it. The earlier 0.24.28 run on the same PC used the same prompt with a different random seed and took 143.3 seconds.
